issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares numberOfLecturers as int, but the solution implementation declares the field numberOfLecturers as byte and its setter/constructor use byte while the getter returns int. This type inconsistency between the specification and the solution (and between field and accessor signatures in the solution) can confuse students who are instructed to follow the UML and may expect an int for numberOfLecturers.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the types with the UML/specification. Change the solution's numberOfLecturers field and related constructor/setter parameter types to int (and have the getter return int), or alternatively update the problem statement/UML to explicitly use byte. Prefer keeping int in code and UML to match the specification and avoid surprising narrow types.
